problems.title: The one-compartment solver returns NaN when ka equals CL/V
problems.summary: For a depot bolus, the central amount has a finite limit at equal absorption and elimination rates. The analytical solver lost precision near equality and returned NaNs at equality, including in derivatives and steady state.

commits.title: onecpt: closed-form solution valid at ka == k10
onecpt test: unit finite-difference step for the amount gradient

fix.why_together: The first commit supplies the one-compartment propagator and regression cases. The second keeps an existing steady-state dose-gradient test accurate under the new formula by using a larger finite-difference step for a quantity linear in dose. The open upstream PR includes both.

validation.detail: At 1bc623ff03, all 10 cases passed, including event tables, near equality, steady state and gradients.

problems.title: Two-compartment and effect-compartment solvers fail at coincident rates
problems.summary: With CL=5, Q=2.5, V2=10 and V3=5, the two disposition rates are 1 and 0.25. Setting ka to either gives nonfinite results. The effect-compartment models have additional singularities, including ka=Q/V3 in the two-compartment effect model.

commits.title: cpt models: closed-form solutions valid where rates coincide
onecpt test: tolerances at the comparisons' own error floor

fix.why_together: The first commit extends the divided-difference propagator to the three additional models. The second adjusts inherited one-compartment comparisons for the shared formula’s rounding error. Apply after the one-compartment pair. The October 19 comment on the open PR describes these additional models.

validation.detail: At 1bc623ff03, all 8 cases passed. They compare divided differences and transient and steady-state values and gradients against independent matrix-exponential references.

problems.title: The one-compartment effect model gives the wrong steady-state effect amount
problems.summary: At distinct rates, an overlapping infusion into the depot can give an effect-compartment amount of 10.80 even though repeated transient infusions converge to 40.50. The steady-state inverse eigenvector matrix had an incorrect last row.

commits.title: cpt models: closed-form solutions valid where rates coincide
onecpt test: tolerances at the comparisons' own error floor

fix.why_together: The same shared propagator that handles coincident rates replaces the faulty steady-state solve. Apply this pair once if also taking the rate-collision fix. The open PR’s October 19 comment reports this distinct-rate example explicitly.

validation.detail: Both cases passed at 1bc623ff03. The tests include separated rates and compare against an independently computed steady state.

problems.title: Feature: Solve constant-delay equations with Torsten dosing events
problems.summary: pmx_solve_dde_rk45 combines Torsten dosing records with constant delays, event-time derivatives and steady-state dosing. Stan Math supplies the integrator and stanc3 recognizes the Stan function. The full infusion repair below also updates this solver’s event schedule.

requires.name: Resumable constant-delay integrator
requires.why: Provides the DDE integrator and the derivative accessor used for state jumps.

requires.name: Stan signatures for pmx_solve_dde_rk45
requires.why: Needed to call the PMX solver from Stan. The C++ tests call the headers directly.

commits.title: pmx_solve_dde_rk45: PMX DDE solver over the resumable DDE core
pmx_solve_dde_rk45: tests of the delayed dynamics
pmx_solve_dde_rk45: gradients with respect to event times
pmx_solve_dde_rk45 test: event-time gradients through steady-state doses

fix.why_together: These commits add the PMX API and event handling, check delayed dynamics, add steady-state dosing, and propagate and test event-time derivatives. They apply in order on Metrum develop. The entry records the feature as a prerequisite of the complete infusion patch.

validation.detail: All 12 C++ tests passed at 1bc623ff03, including delayed dynamics, sensitivities and steady-state dosing. The Stan compiler was outside this run.

problems.title: Periodic infusions disagree with their steady state when bioavailability differs from one
problems.summary: A repeated RATE-defined infusion and the same schedule initialized at steady state give different depot amounts for F=0.8. The two paths deliver the same total dose over different durations.

draft.title: RATE-defined infusions with F ≠ 1 disagree with their periodic steady state

commits.title: F on RATE-defined infusions: keep RATE, last F * AMT / RATE (NONMEM)
Coupled solvers keep a step's start-time sensitivity; F tests at kinks

fix.why_together: The first commit aligns transient and steady-state dosing. The second preserves coupled-solver gradients when an infusion end moves and adjusts finite-difference tests. The complete first commit also updates the DDE solver. To port the schedule alone to upstream develop, apply its diff for ev_history.hpp, ev_manager.hpp, ev_solver.hpp, test/unit/events_test.cpp and test/unit/pmx_ss_biovar_infusion_test.cpp. This five-file subset applies independently of DDE and the analytical repairs.

validation.detail: Upstream bb8266ea printed 0.150748 at steady state and 0.822919 after repeated dosing.
At 1bc623ff03 the reproducer printed 0.150748 twice and all 9 regression tests passed.
On upstream bb8266ea with just the five-file scheduling patch, the reproducer printed 0.150748 twice and the 9 infusion regression tests passed.

problems.title: A lagged dose creates a spurious derivative in the coupled solver
problems.summary: A lagged dose splits the integration interval. The coupled solver lost the derivative of the lower endpoint of the following step, giving even an independent constant-slope response a nonzero derivative with respect to the lag.

draft.title: pmx_solve_onecpt_rk45 gives a nonzero lag derivative for a response independent of the dose

commits.title: Coupled solvers keep a step's start-time sensitivity; F tests at kinks

fix.why_together: This commit applies directly on upstream develop. For the lag-only fix, take pmx_coupled_model.hpp and the additional lag regression in test/unit/coupled_twocpt_typed_test.cpp. The other test changes in the same commit concern the infusion convention. The lag fix does not require DDE or the infusion change.

validation.detail: Upstream bb8266ea gave response 1 and lag derivative 1.
At 1bc623ff03, all 80 typed tests passed. The constant-slope example gave response 1 and lag derivative 0.
On upstream bb8266ea with just pmx_coupled_model.hpp and its lag regression, the reproducer printed 1 0 and all 80 coupled-solver tests passed.
